title: The first run after a rebuild can hang in the terminal colour query
body:
At startup coax asks the terminal for its colours (`palette::query_terminal`, 8c3b646). It puts the terminal in raw mode, writes OSC 10, OSC 11 and DA1 queries, and reads the replies from stdin with `poll` and a 100 ms limit. On Jack's first run after a rebuild, coax showed nothing for 27 seconds. The run's log has `config` at 01:32:10.079 and `agent.start` at 01:32:37.076, and the query is the only code between them. Pressing Ctrl+C, which reaches coax as a byte on stdin in raw mode, ended the wait and the picker appeared. Other runs spent 0 to 0.1 s there. The time must have gone into one blocking system call, either the `read` after `poll` or the write of the queries. Neither the log nor a retry shows which.

## Proposal

- Stdin is non-blocking for the length of the query, so a `read` returns at once, whatever `poll` reported. Its old mode comes back afterwards.
- The log records the query's start before the write, and at the end the bytes read, the time taken and whether the reply or the time limit ended it.
- A test drives the reading loop over a pipe.
